title: console-observability-triage-scratchpad-ari-2026-03-03
content:
Quick triage notes (working scratchpad) - obs dashboard issues reported by customer ACME Corp

Context:
- Date/time observed: 2026-03-03 ~11:30-12:15 UTC (multiple reports)
- Symptoms: several dashboard widgets (route latency heatmap, token-cost breakdown) rendering blank or show "no data"; other widgets load slowly. Intermittent 502s surfaced in UI console logs.
- Affected customers: ACME Corp (support ticket CONS-452), internal QA cluster also saw similar behavior.
- Recent changes: frontend release v2.14.1 rolled out to canary 2026-03-02, backend metrics-aggregator v1.5.0 deployed 2026-03-03 10:00 UTC (auto rollout).

Immediate observations:
- Sentry/console errors: SENTRY-OBS-7892 shows fetch errors to /api/metrics/aggregate with 502 from aggregator pods.
- K8s: aggregator deployment shows 5/8 pods ready for a brief window; rest OOMKilled around 10:05 UTC then restarted.
- Prometheus: spike in scrape latencies for aggregator job at ~10:00-10:10 UTC; CPU usage jumped to 95% for 30s.
- CDN/cache: frontend reported 304s sometimes, but main failure path is 502 from backend, so likely not CDN.

Hypothesis (priority order):
1) Aggregator v1.5.0 has a memory regression causing OOMKilled and returning 502s under certain sequences of grouping queries. Explains OOMs and blank widgets.
2) Canary frontend v2.14.1 might request slightly different aggregation payloads (bigger group_by) exposing the aggregator bug.
3) Autoscaler/HPAs didn't scale quickly enough for short burst, causing backlog.

Immediate TODOs (short):
- [ ] (Ari) Rollback metrics-aggregator to v1.4.8 on canary/qa to confirm regression (due: 2026-03-03 EOD). Ticket: CONS-453 created for rollback plan.
- [ ] (Maya) Add memory usage instrumentation on aggregator (heap histo + max RSS) and increase retention of flame graphs for 24h (due: 2026-03-04).
- [ ] (Jordan) Run targeted load test against aggregator with frontend payload shape from v2.14.1 (script: perf/agg_load_test.sh) and capture OOM reproduction steps (due: 2026-03-03 end of day).
- [ ] (Ari) Add temporary circuit breaker in frontend for aggregator endpoint to fall back to cached summaries (opt for stale-while-revalidate UX) - quick patch if rollback delayed.
- [ ] (All) Postmortem skeleton: collect logs, pod restarts, traces, Sentry stacktraces (assign to postmortem doc after initial triage).

Notes/commands to run:
- k get pods -n observability | grep aggregator  # check restarts and OOMKilled
- kubectl logs deploy/metrics-aggregator -n observability --since=2h | grep "OOMKilled"
- curl -v -X POST https://staging.console/api/metrics/aggregate -d @examples/frontend-v2.14.1-payload.json (run from perf box)
- Perf script: ./perf/agg_load_test.sh --payload examples/frontend-v2.14.1-payload.json --rps 50 --duration 5m

Customer comms (short):
- ACME support update (Ari): "We've triaged the issue and are rolling back a recent backend change while we investigate. Expecting a mitigation within 1 hour. We'll follow up once we have a root cause." (send via support ticket CONS-452 + slack @acct-eng)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q: Did any other services call aggregator with new query shapes? (check service logs for larger group_by queries)
- Q: Is there any recent change in Prometheus scrape config that could cause larger label cardinality? (ask infra)
- Follow-up: confirm whether canary frontend induces larger payloads vs prod frontend. If yes, coordinate with frontend eng to revert or patch.

Longer-term actions to add to backlog (not for immediate):
- Add aggregator resource-safety limits and a QoS tiering; graceful degrade if memory creeps up.
- Add canary traffic shaping so canary frontend can't send full prod traffic patterns to newly deployed backends without extended observation window.
- Add automated regression tests for aggregation memory usage (unit+integration perf tests).

References / artifacts:
- Support ticket: CONS-452 (ACME reports)
- Rollback ticket: CONS-453 (rollback plan + owner Ari)
- Sentry errors: SENTRY-OBS-7892
- PR to review: github:org/repo/pull/234 (aggregator v1.5.0 changes)

Quick log of actions taken:
- 11:45 UTC: reached out to infra to confirm OOM events (Maya)
- 12:05 UTC: started targeted load test (Jordan)
- 12:30 UTC: opened rollback ticket CONS-453 (Ari)

Scratch TODO (personal):
- remind @frontend-team to include payload-size telemetry in next release notes
- check billing impact if dashboard polling rates increased for impacted customers

End of scratchpad - keep this doc for triage timeline + copy into postmortem doc later.
